title: Why the World Still Needs Wall Street
gist: Despite mounting reasons to diversify away from the US, the dollar still dominates global reserves and FX trading because no other financial system can absorb comparable capital inflows, meaning geopolitical multipolarity is outpacing financial multipolarity.

insights.claim: Investors have multiple structural reasons to diversify away from US assets, including rising US public debt, deepening political polarization, unpredictable trade policy, doubts about the rule of law, and financial sanctions that have pushed other governments toward dollar alternatives.
insights.speaker: Jorge Arbache
insights.so_what: Lists the specific catalysts an investor should track as potential drivers of a slow-motion shift away from dollar assets, even though it hasn't happened yet.
insights.quote: America’s public debt is rising, political polarization is deepening, trade policy has become unpredictable, the rule of law is now in doubt, and financial sanctions have encouraged other governments to seek alternatives to the dollar.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “BRASÍLIA—Investors have no shortage of reasons”

insights.claim: Despite the reasons to diversify, there has been no great exodus from US financial markets to date.
insights.speaker: Jorge Arbache
insights.so_what: Confirms that dollar-diversification remains a thesis rather than an observed capital flow trend, cautioning against overweighting de-dollarization narratives in near-term positioning.
insights.quote: Yet there has been no great exodus from US markets.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “BRASÍLIA—Investors have no shortage of reasons”

insights.claim: The US dollar accounted for 56.8% of allocated global foreign-exchange reserves at the end of 2025.
insights.speaker: Jorge Arbache
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark reserve-currency investors and central banks can use to track de-dollarization progress over coming quarters.
insights.quote: The dollar still accounted for 56.8% of allocated foreign-exchange reserves at the end of 2025
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “BRASÍLIA—Investors have no shortage of reasons”

insights.claim: The US dollar was used in 89.2% of all foreign-exchange trades surveyed by the Bank for International Settlements.
insights.speaker: Jorge Arbache
insights.so_what: Underscores how entrenched the dollar remains in FX trading infrastructure, a key headwind to any near-term multipolar currency shift.
insights.quote: was used in 89.2% of all foreign-exchange trades surveyed by the Bank for International Settlements
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “BRASÍLIA—Investors have no shortage of reasons”

insights.claim: Geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity because financial systems outside the United States face major constraints on their ability to absorb large capital inflows.
insights.speaker: Jorge Arbache
insights.so_what: Offers a structural explanation for why rival financial centers (e.g., China, EU) cannot yet displace Wall Street even as global politics fragments — a key constraint for any reserve-currency diversification thesis.
insights.quote: Outside of the United States, all other financial systems face major constraints on their ability to absorb large financial inflows. That is why geopolitical multipolarity is advancing faster than financial multipolarity
